We also looked at court-filing defect checks: the Supreme Court already uses an AI tool built with IIT Madras, and a commercial tool is reported in 16 High Courts, so we chose the problem nobody automates yet: checking a question paper and its translations.
IndicDoc AI | Phase-2: Project Implementation4
WHAT WE SOLVE

Problem Statement and Objectives

Problem: a question paper is set in one language and translated into Hindi and regional languages. Every version is checked by hand before printing. When a number, an option, a mark or a whole question differs, lakhs of candidates are affected: grace marks, re-exams, court cases.
MAIN OBJECTIVE

Build an offline deep-learning system that reads a printed paper in any of 12 Indian languages and flags every structural or numerical error, and every difference from its source version, before printing.

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES
  • Detect the paper's structure (questions, options, answers) with a layout detector; compare 3 detectors.
  • Read text with reliable numbers in 12 languages (number pass).
  • Checks: numbering, duplicates, options, marks, translation parity, repeats, format profiles.
  • Measure errors found and false alarms on a benchmark; ship app + API in Docker.
EXPECTED OUTPUT

A verdict (print / check / do not print) and each finding with its question and page, outlined on the page, as HTML and JSON.

IT HAS ALREADY HAPPENED

APPSC Group-I51 of 120 questions alleged mistranslated into Telugu; SC notice

OUR APPROACH

Proposed System, Methodology and Novelty

1
Paper inPDF / scans + source version
2
Find structureDocLayout-YOLO: questions, options
3
Read textIndic OCR + English number pass
4
Build questionsnumber, stem, options, marks, figures
5
Checkstructure, parity, repeats, format
6
Reportverdict + findings on the page
How deep learning is used
A convolutional object detector finds every question, sub-question, option and answer on the page (AP@50 0.81–0.90 on these labels). Its regions and the word positions inside them turn a picture of a page into structured questions, in any script.
What is new
Translation parity without translation: numbers, option counts, marks, sub-questions and figures must be the same in every language, so versions are compared question by question with no MT model.
Number pass: two OCR models must agree on every digit.
Why it sells
USP: no tool we found checks an Indian question paper against its translations question by question; IndicDoc Verify does, offline, in 12 languages, before printing. Confidential papers never leave the exam body. Same engine checks any document format via JSON profiles (e.g. bilingual circulars).

DATA

Dataset Description and Pre-processing

Layout dataIndicDLP (Nath et al., ICDAR 2025; Hugging Face ai4bharat/indicdlp, AIKosh): 119,806 pages, 12 languages, 12 domains, 42 labels
Our subset3,317 pages, 49,995 boxes, language-balanced, official splits: train 2,293 · val 342 · test 682. 195 question-paper pages; 1,227 question and 1,209 option boxes
Verify benchmark132 paper pairs (English → Hindi, English → Tamil), 18 questions each (MCQ + short answer), rendered at 200 dpi; 108 with one injected error of 9 real kinds, 24 clean; half degraded like scans
Kept apartA separate development set (48 pairs, other seed) was used to build the parser; the test set above was run once
Pre-processingParquet → PNG + COCO JSON; boxes clipped; COCO → YOLO labels; letterbox 640 / 1024 px. Verify: PDF → 200 dpi; blur 0.7 px + noise σ 8 + JPEG 55 for "scanned"
AugmentationYOLOv8: mosaic, HSV, scale. Faster R-CNN: colour jitter, blur. No mirror flips
ChallengesClass imbalance ("paragraph" = 32% of boxes); no OCR ground truth in IndicDLP; no public set of erroneous exam papers, hence the benchmark
Deliverabledataset/ CSVs + samples; scripts/verify_bench/ rebuilds the benchmark

WHAT WE BUILT

Implementation Details

  • Layout model: COCO-pretrained YOLOv8s and Faster R-CNN fine-tuned (SGD 0.005 / auto, CIoU+DFL+BCE), DocLayout-YOLO used for verification at its high-recall threshold (0.15).
  • OCR: the page is read once with its own script's model; an English number pass fixes misread Latin digits (Hindi reads "1947" as "947") and the two must agree on every number.
  • Questions: question regions start a question; options are separated by layout gaps between words, so garbled markers do not matter; marks, figures, tables attached.
  • Checks: numbering, duplicates, option count, marks total; parity by global alignment (Needleman–Wunsch) on language-independent features; repeats by character 3-gram similarity; format profiles in JSON.
  • Output: verdict, findings with question and page, problems outlined on the page; HTML / JSON; same code in app, API and benchmark.
# every page: layout (DL) -> OCR with number pass
out = predict_single(model, page, "doclayout", device, conf=0.15)
doc = extract_document(page, out, "hin", number_pass=True)

# ml/verify — questions, checks, parity, repeats
report = verify(hindi_pages, source_pages=english_pages,
                bank=earlier_questions, profile="question_paper")
report["summary"]   # {questions, errors, warnings}
html = to_html(report, {"paper": page_images})

LESSONS

Challenges and Limitations

OCR is the weakest link
Indic Tesseract models misread Latin digits ("1947" → "947", "1" → "।") and glue option markers to values. The number pass, layout-based option splitting and page-level digit-script detection were needed to get false alarms down.
No public data of real errors
Exam bodies do not publish erroneous pre-print papers, so we built a benchmark with realistic injected errors, kept a separate development set, and report clean and scan-degraded results separately.
Meaning is not checked yet
Parity catches numbers, options, marks and missing questions without translation. A pure change of meaning (a dropped word) needs a cross-lingual model; there is a hook for one, not yet evaluated.
Compute and data size
Our own detectors saw 2.3K pages for an hour (0.26 vs 0.76 mAP@50 for the released model); the product therefore uses the released model, and our work is the checker built on it.

WRAP-UP

Conclusion and Future Scope

CONCLUSION
  • Implemented: IndicDoc Verify — layout detection (3 detectors compared), OCR for 12 scripts with a number pass, question parsing, structure / parity / repeat / format checks, report, web app, REST API, Docker.
  • Results: 98% of injected errors found at the right question on born-digital papers (98% on degraded scans), 3.0 false alarms per clean born-digital pair; best layout model 0.759 mAP@50.
  • Objectives: all four met. Our own detectors did not reach the released model, which we report openly.
SELLING IT
  • Buyers: NTA, UPSC and state PSCs, school boards, university exam cells, test-series publishers; offline licence per exam body.
FUTURE SCOPE
  • Pilot with a university exam cell or a state board on real pre-print papers; measure minutes saved per paper.
  • Meaning check with a cross-lingual sentence model; number words and formulas.
  • Better Indic OCR behind the same interface; answer-key consistency check.
  • More document profiles: bilingual government circulars (Official Languages Act s.3(3)), forms, certificates.
